OTE · Optimal Trade Entry · Living Course

OTE — the Golden Pocket

Markets don't move in straight lines — every trend leg retraces to fill orders before continuing. OTE is knowing, in advance, where that retrace lands: a Fibonacci zone called the Golden Pocket (0.705–0.786), entered with a tight stop for 1:4 to 1:20+ asymmetry. The entire edge is patience — "OTE exists to help you practice patience."

SOURCES · ell.funded — "How I top & bottom tick the market using OTE" · ell.funded — 192-pt recap (OTE × STDV pairing + the CE) · Dylan — the 3m marking strat, the rolling .705 anchor & the fallback ladder · lineage: Matthew Scriv · builds alongside the ICC course as sources are studied

STEP 1

Bias

Draw the OTE on the higher timeframe (15m/1H/daily). The active cycle IS the bias — and it holds until the cycle completes.

→
STEP 2

Wait

Price must come to the 0.705. If the structure is valid, it will — entering early at the 0.5 or a random FVG murders the R-multiple.

→
STEP 3

Enter with confluence

Golden Pocket tap + at least one ally: STDV level, inverse FVG, rejection block, SMT. Stop between the 0.786 and the 1. Target through the 0.

SOURCE 1 · ELL.FUNDED · TOP & BOTTOM TICKING

One zone, one trigger: 0.705

The fib gets exactly these levels — 0 · 0.5 · 0.705 · 0.786 · 1 — and only one zone matters. The 0.5 is the breakeven line where impatient traders leak their edge; the 0.705 is the trigger he acts on for every entry. Same 30-tick stop, entered at 0.705 instead of 0.5, turns a 0.8R trade into a 1:5.

enter ONLY the Golden Pocket — 0.705 to 0.786
stop between the 0.786 and the 1 · target through the 0
tap 0.705 → the cycle completes ONLY when the 0 breaks
FIB SETTINGS: 0 · 0.5 · 0.705 · 0.786 · 1 — NOTHING ELSE · THE 0.5 IS A TRAP FOR THE IMPATIENT
1

The draw — wick to body, not wick to wick

The Matthew Scriv anchoring method: top anchor on the wick high, bottom anchor on the BODY of the lowest-wick candle — not its wick. The refined zone this produces is the whole trick. As the trend extends and a new extreme prints, shift the anchor to the new candle's wick-body and redraw — the OTE walks down the trend with price, leg by leg.

2

Cycle completion IS the bias

Once price taps the 0.705, the cycle is armed — and it only completes when the 0 breaks. Until that break, the directional bias holds, full stop. This rule kept him bearish NQ for a week and a half through every scary bounce — worth 5,000 ticks. The moment the 0 broke after a low-to-high swing, the bias flipped bullish and the next OTE was drawn the other way. No feelings, no news — the cycle is the opinion.

3

Two altitudes — HTF bias, LTF trigger 15M/1H → 3M

The high-timeframe OTE (15m/1H/daily) sets the macro bias and the major retracement targets. The 3-minute OTE prices the actual entry inside it. The overnight NQ rep: 3m Golden Pocket tap + a 15m inverse fair value gap + a standard-deviation level stacked at the same price — 30-tick stop, 1:5 paid. Same framework at every scale; only the stop size changes.

4

Confluence multiplies, never replaces

OTE alone is the skeleton; the allies confirm the zone: standard-deviation levels (a −4 SD landing on the pocket), inverse FVGs on the 3–15m, rejection blocks, and SMT divergence (NQ makes the low, correlated MNQ/ES doesn't — the reversal tell). On high-liquidity days the stack goes vertical: CPI-day pockets offered 1:50 to 1:70 setups to whoever waited. At least one ally aligned with the pocket before entry — that's the floor.

The settings are the settings. 0 · 0.5 · 0.705 · 0.786 · 1. Wrong levels = you literally cannot see the pocket.
0.705 is the trigger. The pocket is 0.705–0.786, and the first number is where the order goes. The 0.5 entry is how a 1:5 becomes a 0.8:1.
Anchors: wick high → body of the lowest wick. And they MOVE — every new extreme re-anchors the fib down (or up) the trend.
The cycle rules the bias. Tap 0.705 → hold direction until the 0 breaks → then flip and redraw. Bounces inside an incomplete cycle are noise, not reversals.
One confluence ally minimum. STDV · inverse FVG · rejection block · SMT — something else must point at the pocket before the entry exists.
30% win rate pays. His first prop payouts came losing 7 of 10 — the pocket's tight stop against 1:4–1:20 targets means the math never needed him to be right often. Patience is the position.
🎯How OTE plugs into the house system. OTE is the WHERE refinement inside the ICC cascade — ICC diagnoses the trend and the level, and the Golden Pocket prices exactly where the correction should die: it's the "second time around" entry measured with a fib instead of an eyeball. The cycle-completion rule is ICC's previous-push invalidation wearing numbers. Astro stays the WHEN layer — nothing here changes the weather doctrine. SOURCE 2 · ELL.FUNDED · THE 192-PT RECAP — OTE × STDV

The pocket without the ladder is a coin flip

The Feb 18–19 NQ top-tick answers the biggest question about OTE: when do you take the pocket, and when do you wait? He drew a textbook OTE, entered it clean — and got stopped. Not because OTE failed, but because the STDV ladder wasn't done: the midnight manipulation leg's −4 sat just overhead, and the algorithm doesn't leave a −4 unpaid. The pairing doctrine in one line: OTE names the zone — STDV tells you if the zone is ripe.

FVG CE rejections build the BIAS · the OTE draw names the ZONE
the active STDV ladder VALIDATES the zone — an unpaid −4 overhead means the pocket is EARLY
enter at the −4 tap + rejection · target the NEW leg's ladder through −4
CE = CONSEQUENT ENCROACHMENT — THE 50% MIDPOINT OF A FAIR VALUE GAP (OR A WICK: "WICKS ARE GAPS")
📖What the CE actually is. Every fair value gap has a midpoint — the Consequent Encroachment, its 50% line. That line is the imbalance's verdict level: rejection at the CE means the gap is still in control (bias holds); a candle close through the CE means the level is failing. Same logic applies to big wicks — a wick is just a gap that got filled fast, so its 50% is a CE too. It's the precision line inside every zone: the 4H FVG's CE said "still bearish," the 1H FVG's CE said it again, and that 1H CE landing exactly on the 0.705 is what made the pocket a real level and not a hope.
1

Top-down bias: CE → CE → pocket 4H → 1H → 5M

A big 4H range-move down leaves a 4H FVG; price comes back up and rejects its CE — the market isn't ready to go up. Drop to the 1H: an untapped FVG, CE rejected again, no candle close above. Bias = lower. Only then draw the 5m OTE from the range high to low — and note the kicker: the 1H FVG's CE sits exactly on the 0.705. Two independent tools naming one price.

THE ZONE · Fib from the range high→low on the 5m. 0.5 is where the market rebalances; the 0.705 is the premium entry he's stalking. Everything below is chop he refuses to touch — "I'm not in premium."
THE CE CONFLUENCE · The 1H FVG box overhead — its 50% (the CE) lands exactly on the 0.705. When a gap's midpoint and the golden pocket agree, that price is a level, not a wish.
2

The stop-out — and why the pocket was early

Price taps the level, rejects, gives an inverse FVG — he enters the OTE with stops at the high. Stopped out. The chart wasn't wrong; the ladder wasn't finished. Pull up midnight open (12 AM EST), mark the manipulation leg wick low → body high, print the STDV levels — and there it is: the −4 of the midnight leg sitting just above the entry. The algorithm wanted its max extension first. "Maybe we did want the negative four."

❌ THE DONT · The clean-looking pocket entry that died. Rule from the loss: never take the OTE blind — check the active STDV projection first. An unpaid −4 overhead flips the pocket from entry to bait.
THE DIAGNOSIS LAYER · Midnight open (12 AM EST) + manipulation leg keyed wick low → body high. This is the STDV precision layer that explains the stop-out before it becomes a tilt spiral.
3

Enter where the ladder ends: the −4 top-tick

Price runs up and taps the midnight leg's −4 to the tick — rejection — short. Stop ~10 points, not 8: he gives it room for the CE sitting right above ("just in case it wants to come up and hit that — you're just letting it breathe"). A tighter stop is a bigger R, but the top-tick doesn't need to be squeezed. That's the full marriage: OTE zone + CE line + STDV max extension = the entry.

−4 TO THE TICK · The midnight ladder's max extension caps the move exactly where the fib said it would. The "failed" OTE entry was just one rung early.
THE BUY-IN · Short at the −4 rejection with breathing room over the CE. One micro on a funded account with $25 of drawdown left — conviction from confluence, not size.
4

Target the next ladder, manage at true day open

Where's the take-profit? Key the new manipulation leg (the pop up into −4, then the dump): wick high → body low — checked against the 5m so it spans the whole leg. Fake liquidity below gets wiped en route ("it wants to wipe that out before going anywhere"). Personal target: that leg's −4 max extension, because the 0.705 of a big range broke — the market goes way lower. For the add: watch true day open (the midnight EST candle open) — a rejection there is the structured re-entry, not a chase.

THE PAYOFF · Riding the new ladder down: open P&L +147, tool reading RR 63.75, target 191 at the downside −4. Final print: 192 points, ~1:19–1:20 realized. Straight top tick.
TRUE DAY OPEN RE-ENTRY · The retrace tags the midnight-EST candle open — a draw-on-liquidity level that doubles as the re-entry rejection spot for adding size in premium.
THE WHOLE MODEL ON ONE SCREEN · Up-leg ladder paying its −4 (the top tick), then the down-leg ladder delivering 192 points through −2.5/−3/−4. Two fibs, one algorithm, zero guessing.
Check the ladder before the pocket. An OTE tap while an active projection's −4 is unpaid overhead = early. Let the max extension print, then strike.
CE = the gap's 50%. Rejection at CE → imbalance holds, bias holds. Close through CE → the level's failing. Works on FVGs and big wicks alike.
CE + 0.705 stacked = a real level. When the gap midpoint lands on the golden pocket, two tools name one price — that's the tap worth waiting hours for.
Give the stop room for the CE. 10 points instead of 8 at a top-tick is cheap insurance — the level above your entry gets to breathe, your R barely notices.
Exit plan = the NEXT leg's ladder. Entry comes off one projection's ending; targets come from the new manipulation leg's ladder — partial the zones, max at −4.
A stop-out is data. The OTE loss didn't trigger revenge — it triggered the midnight markup that found the real level. Ask the chart why, then re-enter better.
🔗The full pairing, condensed. ICC reads the story · FVG CEs vote on bias · OTE names the zone · STDV decides if the zone is ripe and prices the exit · SMT and true day open referee the turns. This is the same trade documented from the STDV side in the STDV guide's worked example — two lenses, one 192-point delivery. Study it from both.
SOURCE 3 · DYLAN — THE 3M MARKING STRAT · THE ROLLING ANCHOR · THE FALLBACK LADDER

Mark it on the 3m, roll it at the .705

Dylan's refinement pins the draw to one timeframe and makes the anchor-shifting rule mechanical. The OTE is marked on the 3-minute: fib 1 on the tick high (the exact wick extreme), fib 0 on the BODY of the lowest-wick candle. And the moment price taps the 0.705 and dips, that rejection swing IS the next fib's 1 — the OTE chains itself down the trend, leg by leg, with zero discretion about where the next draw starts.

draw on the 3M · fib 1 = TICK HIGH · fib 0 = BODY of the lowest-wick candle
price taps the 0.705 and dips → that swing becomes the NEXT fib's 1 — roll and redraw
retrace dies BELOW the pocket → fallback levels 0.5 · 0.618 · 0.66 — only WITH a rejection level
STRONGEST STACK: REJECTION LEVEL (FVG · ORDER BLOCK · REJECTION BLOCK) + OTE POCKET + STDV −4 TO −4.5 AT ONE PRICE
1

The 3m draw — tick high to the lowest wick's body 3M

Source 1 taught the anchors; Dylan pins the altitude. The marking chart is the 3-minute — precise enough to anchor the exact tick high, coarse enough that the swings are real. Bearish draw: 1 on the tick high, 0 on the BODY of the lowest-wick candle (mirror it for longs: tick low → body of the highest wick). The 15m/1H OTE still frames the macro bias — but the fib that prices the entry lives on the 3m.

2

The rolling anchor — the .705 dip IS the next 1

Source 1 said "anchors move" — this is the trigger that moves them. When price comes up, taps the 0.705, and dips, that tap-and-rejection swing is the trend confirming the pocket held. Don't wait for a new extreme to redraw: that rejection high becomes the 1 of the next fib, its leg runs to the new lowest-wick body, and the next golden pocket prints automatically. Chained pockets = the trend's own rhythm, drawn in advance, every leg.

3

The fallback ladder — when the market can't reach the pocket

Strong days retrace shallow. If price rejects below the 0.705–0.786 and can't push further up, the pocket may never get tapped — that weakness is itself information. Dylan's fallback: watch the 0.5, 0.618, and 0.66 for the entry instead. But the shallow levels are never taken naked: they only count when a rejection level — an FVG, an order block, or a rejection block — sits on them. The pocket needs one ally; a fallback level needs a bodyguard.

4

The full Dylan stack — rejection level + pocket + ladder end

The strongest setup he names is the triple overlap: a rejection level (FVG / OB / rejection block) landing inside the 0.705–0.786 while the active STDV ladder's −4 to −4.5 completes at the same price. Three independent tools, one price — the same "two tools naming one price" law from Source 2, with the discretion layer stacked on top. Which rejection level qualifies, and when to trust it, is the MD guide's whole subject.

The 3m is the marking chart. Tick high → body of the lowest wick, drawn where the ticks are visible. HTF frames bias; the 3m prices entries.
Tap + dip = roll. The .705 rejection swing is the next fib's 1. No waiting, no eyeballing — the chain draws itself.
Rejection below the pocket = shallow-retrace regime. Shift attention to 0.5 / 0.618 / 0.66 — with a rejection level on them, or no trade.
Add 0.618 · 0.66 to the preset as fallback lines. The pocket stays the A+ entry; the fallback ladder is for days too strong to fill it.
The triple stack is the A++: rejection level + golden pocket + STDV −4/−4.5 at one price. That's the setup worth sitting on your hands for.
Drawings are the journal. Keep the position tool and every fib on the chart — the running record IS the review (Dylan's rule).
🧭Where discretion enters. The marking is now mechanical — 3m anchors, rolling .705, fallback ladder. What's NOT mechanical is judging the level: is the FVG displaced and unviolated? Is the rejection block's wick fib holding? Is this chop? That judgment layer is Market Discretion — the MD tab — built from Dylan's advice and the house's full toolkit.
